descricao_original: By electron microscopy, the details of the interalveolar septum are more evident, particularly the cytology of a type II (septal) cell. Septal cells secrete surfactant, a mixture of phospholipids and protein. The secretory granules (vesicles) are often referred to as lamellar bodies, due to their lipid content. One granule in the process of exocytosis is visible. 4000x
